transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Um, hi. I guess I came in because I’ve just been really tired lately—probably sounds kind of small, sorry—but it’s getting hard to get through my shifts. My body feels… heavy, like it’s filled with wet sand, and even when I rest, I don’t really feel like I bounce back.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but things I usually really like just feel kind of… flat. Like cooking for myself, playing guitar, going hiking, even going over to my family’s place. I still know I should care, and I kind of go through the motions, but it feels like I’m pretending more than actually enjoying it. Is that what you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… I think it’s been about four months, if I’m counting right. The really low, empty feeling started after that first burst of energy I had at work kind of faded, and it just… didn’t really go away. I kept thinking it would pass, so I didn’t want to make a big deal of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

A little, yeah. I mean, not in a dramatic way or anything, but my appetite’s been kind of all over the place. Lately I mostly just… forget to eat, or I’ll make something and it tastes like cardboard, so I don’t finish it. My work pants have been fitting looser too, so I guess I’ve probably lost some weight without really trying. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have trouble sitting still and feel restless?

Yeah… kind of both, at different times. Earlier on I was, um, probably a little too restless at work—pacing around the store, straightening shelves over and over, just keeping myself moving. I didn’t think it was that bad.

But lately it’s more the opposite. Even walking to the bus feels like I’m moving through mud, and if someone asks me something, it takes me a second to answer. I don’t know if that counts, but it feels slower and heavier than normal.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or would you ever consider ending your life?

I… I don’t think I would actually do anything, or I don’t want to scare anyone. But yeah, I’ve had some thoughts that scared me. Like maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up.

And a few times walking home, I caught myself thinking about just… stepping off the curb into traffic. I haven’t told anyone that because it sounds awful. Is that… is that the kind of thing you need to know?
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or so good that others might have noticed you were acting out of character? Even for just a few days?

Yeah… I guess there was a stretch like that. I don’t know if I’d call it “high,” exactly, but I felt really good—like extra cheerful, like I could handle anything, almost unstoppable.

People probably noticed, honestly. I was more upbeat than usual. But then I’d also get kind of… sharp. Like if someone asked me to count a drawer again at work, I’d snap way harder than I should have. It wasn’t my best moment. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
How long did you feel that way during that stretch when you felt unusually good and extra cheerful?

Um… I think it’s been about a month, maybe? Since the store changed our hours for the remodel. That’s when I really noticed I was feeling different.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but yeah, around a month sounds right. Is that helpful?
During that time when you felt unusually good and extra cheerful, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual—like you could go with much less sleep but still feel energetic?

Yeah… I mean, I guess so. With the shift changes, I started sleeping only a few hours some nights, and I’d still feel kind of wired the next day, like I didn’t really need more.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but even now when I’m really tired, I’ll wake up early and my mind is already going. Does that count?

During the time you felt unusually good and extra cheerful, did you find yourself doing things much more quickly or intensely than usual—like taking on a lot of tasks at once, talking faster, or feeling like you couldn’t slow down?

Yeah… I mean, I was definitely more “on,” I guess. I kept volunteering for extra cash-office stuff at work, and then I’d start reorganizing shelves like it suddenly had to be fixed right then.

I also made this whole promotion binder… which sounds productive, I know, but it was probably a little much. And then I’d go home and still feel like I needed to do something, like shop online or rearrange my apartment. I don’t know if that’s what you mean by not slowing down, but it kind of felt like that.
